claims.text: The baseline FeCoNiCrAl feedstock has a particle-size range of 15–45 μm.
Conventional thermal-spray deposition of this feedstock produces a sub-target bond-coat thickness.
The proposed intervention is injection-directed high-velocity air-fuel spraying with a propylene-fueled i7 torch.
The proposed ID-HVAF configuration provides lower thermal input than the conventional baseline process.
Lower process temperature preserves the morphology of FeCoNiCrAl particles during spraying.
Lower thermal input reduces premature oxidation of the alloy particles.
Lower thermal input reduces melting-related or thermal degradation of the alloy particles.
Reduced oxidation and thermal degradation increase particle retention after impact.
The proposed process improves cohesion within the deposited coating.
Improved particle retention and cohesion increase deposition efficiency.
The ID-HVAF intervention will produce a thicker coating than the conventional-process baseline.
The resulting bond coat will meet or exceed the required coating thickness.
The thicker ID-HVAF coating will retain the alloy's microstructural integrity relative to the baseline.
The ID-HVAF coating will exhibit minimal as-sprayed oxidation relative to the baseline.
The intervention should remain effective under operating and service conditions typical of thermal-barrier-coating bond coats.

contradictions.description: The main outcome requires meeting or exceeding the unspecified required thickness, whereas the falsification rule treats a greater-than-10% thickness increase as sufficient to avoid thickness-based falsification. A gain above 10% could still leave the coating below the required thickness.
